newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Telstra to pay govt A$3 bln - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Telstra to pay govt A$3 bln - paper.

text.p: Australian state-owned telecommunications group Telstra Corp is planning to pay the government a one-off special dividend of up to A$3 billion before a third of the group is privatised later this year, The Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Monday.
"Senior Telstra figures said yesterday the company board was comfortable with a special dividend payment of between A$2 billion and A$3 billion," the Financial Review said.

"A special dividend, or capital repayment, of this size would help bring down the 'headline' budget deficit, but is not expected to have any significant effect on the underlying deficit," the newspaper said.

Last week Telstra, Australia's largest telecommunications group, reported a net profit after abnormals of A$742.0 million in the six months to December 31, 1996, compared with A$1.20 billion a year ago.
Telstra also announced an interim dividend to the government of A$625 million.
The government passed legislation last year to sell one-third of Telstra by the end of 1997 for a projected A$8.0 billion, but recent estimates put the sale price much higher.

The Financial Review also said Telstra was accelerating plans to sell key assets before it was partly privatised, including some of its property holdings, part of the business that deals with customers' phone equipment and other underperforming areas.
"Senior company officials said these sales could taked place before June 30, in time to be reflected in the company's final full-year result," the newspaper said.
Telstra currently has a debt-equity ratio of 28 percent, which is considered low for most telecommunications companies.
